assessment: The observations do not establish a shortage of total room capacity: acceptable windows, equipment needs and usable attendance remain unknown. Both openings are hypotheses; neither establishes that the eight-week targets are feasible.

openings.claim: Groups may share indispensable musicians, making some nominally separate reservations mutually unusable and contributing to late or missed sessions.
openings.delta: Treat the scheduling unit as compatible group attendance, alongside room availability, rather than assuming each group is independent.
openings.prediction: If shared personnel are a material cause, contacts will identify overlapping indispensable attendance requirements corresponding to late or missed sessions; moving those bookings to acceptable nonoverlapping windows should improve attendance without adding room-hours.
openings.probe: During the available short conversations, ask contacts which other groups share essential attendees and whether this caused any of the 14 affected sessions. Record only group-pair conflicts. If supported, trial one mutually accepted schedule exchange while protecting every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement and the performances; compare attendance at the affected sessions.
assumptions: Some groups may share essential attendees; this is unobserved.
An acceptable exchange exists and can be recorded consistently through existing telephone or desk channels.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: allocating requested 60-minute weekly entitlements before allocating optional extensions can prevent inherited 90-minute bookings from stranding useful rehearsal time.
openings.delta: Separate guaranteed access from additional duration, using stated rehearsal needs to decide extensions rather than inheriting every booking length.
openings.prediction: Where contiguous fragments and acceptable windows align, this allocation admits previously excluded groups while retaining sufficient longer sessions; otherwise it reveals that shortening bookings cannot resolve the bottleneck.
openings.probe: Use contacts' actual duration, window and equipment requirements to draft one weekly allocation within existing staffed hours, preserving performances. Compare satisfied needs and excluded groups with the inherited allocation, and count administration time before any agreed trial. Accept telephone and in-person changes, with one authoritative booking record.
assumptions: Some 90-minute reservations can be shortened without losing required rehearsal value.
A 60-minute entitlement does not by itself count as meeting a group's full stated need.
Guaranteed slots remain available to every requesting group; existing equipment and zero new fees are retained.
